title: Updating & Deleting Records
description: Create edit forms, handle deletes, and use revalidation to keep the UI fresh.

slides.title: Edit and Delete ✏️🗑️
slides.content:
# Beyond Creation

A complete application needs to update and delete existing records.

We'll add two new Server Actions:
* `updatePost(id, formData)`
* `deletePost(id)`

These follow the same pattern: validate (for update), call Prisma, revalidate the path.

We'll also create an edit form that pre‑fills existing data.

slides.title: Update Action (app/actions.js)
slides.content: Similar to create but accepts an ID.

quizData.question: Which Prisma method changes an existing record?
quizData.explanation: `update` takes a `where` clause and the new `data` to modify the record.

slides.title: Delete Action (app/actions.js)
slides.content: A simple delete by ID, then revalidate.

slides.title: Edit Form with Pre‑filled Data 📄
Edit Form Component (components/EditPostForm.js)
slides.content: Client component that uses the update action and shows defaults.

quizData.question: Why do we use `updatePost.bind(null, post.id)`?

options.text: To create a new function with the first argument (id) pre‑filled

quizData.explanation: `.bind()` creates a new function where `id` is already set as the first argument. The form will then pass `prevState` and `formData` after that.

slides.title: Delete with a Button & Confirmation ⚠️
slides.content:
# Safe Deletes

Since `deletePost` doesn't need form data, we can call it directly with a button click using a client component.

```jsx
<button onClick={() => deletePost(post.id)}>Delete</button>
```

But we should add a confirmation dialog:

```jsx
<button onClick={() => {
  if (confirm('Are you sure?')) deletePost(post.id);
}}>Delete</button>
```

After deletion, `revalidatePath` will refresh the list automatically.

slides.title: Optimistic Delete ✨
slides.content: You can use `useOptimistic` to immediately remove the post from the list while the delete action runs. This makes the UI feel instant. If the delete fails, rollback happens automatically.
